newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on crude, China.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on crude, China.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up at midday on Friday as sentiment picked up on firmer overnight crude prices and fresh buying from China at low levels, traders said.
"The market picked up because crude is up and also because the Chinese are buying at lower prices," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $23.40/$23.60, up 20 cents from Thursday with the July/August time spread firmly at minus 20 cents value, brokers said.
Traders said the market discounted earlier concerns of a prompt overhang which forced one refiner to ship cargoes out for storage outside its refinery complex.
The improved sentiment was due to buying interest from several sides at under $23.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for physical cargoes which has put a floor to the recent price fall.
"We saw buying from a local trader when prices fell below $23.00 and the Chinese have also bought cargoes at around this level," a trader said.
Traders said the Chinese have bought afew 30,000-tonne sized cargoes at around $180 per tonne cost-and-freight basis to south China over the past few days.
The local traders who stepped in to buy spot at $22.90 and $23.00 per barrel on Tuesday are expected to buy more cargoes if prices fall again, traders said.
The traders have since March 3 bought well over 22 million barrels but over the past month have slowed their daily purchases to between one or two 150,000-barrel cargoes or even nothing.
As a result of this stocks in Singapore have risen creating a near tank top situation at some refineries.

The high stock level was refleced in data released by the Singapore's Trade Development Board showed that middle distillate stocks have risen by 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels for the week ending June 11.
The stocks are at their highest since at least Janaury 1994.
Fuel oil swaps rose slightly on firmer with July indicated at $99.50/$100.50, up 50 cents from Thursday.
Overnight July Brent crude closed up nine cents to $17.44 per barrel and was last traded up 16 cents to $17.50 on SIMEX.
